report_name: New Stealthy Mirai Variant 'Evooo1Bot' Targets Common Routers

attack_patterns.name: Vulnerability Scanning
attack_patterns.description: The Evooo1Bot botnet actively scans the internet for vulnerable routers to compromise.

attack_patterns.name: Password Guessing
attack_patterns.description: Evooo1Bot attempts to log into target devices by trying a list of common default usernames and passwords, a method inherited from the original Mirai malware.

attack_patterns.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
attack_patterns.description: Evooo1Bot exploits a series of known, unpatched software vulnerabilities in specific router models to gain initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Network Denial of Service
attack_patterns.description: The primary goal of the Evooo1Bot botnet is to launch Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks by flooding a target with traffic from its network of compromised devices.

malware.name: Mirai
malware.description: A malware family that primarily targets online consumer devices such as routers and IP cameras, infecting them to create a botnet used for launching DDoS attacks.

malware.name: Evooo1Bot
malware.description: A new, stealthy variant of the Mirai botnet that spreads by exploiting unpatched vulnerabilities in SOHO routers and brute-forcing default credentials. It includes features to evade detection and make removal more difficult.

identities.name: Alcatel
identities.description: A vendor whose routers are targeted by the Evooo1Bot malware variant.

identities.name: D-Link
identities.description: A vendor whose routers are targeted by the Evooo1Bot malware variant.

identities.name: Netgear
identities.description: A vendor whose routers are targeted by the Evooo1Bot malware variant.

identities.name: Tenda
identities.description: A vendor whose routers are targeted by the Evooo1Bot malware variant.

infrastructure.name: Evooo1Bot C2 Infrastructure
infrastructure.description: Command-and-control (C2) server infrastructure that Evooo1Bot connects to in order to await instructions for DDoS attacks.

indicators.name: Suspicious Outbound Telnet from IoT Device
indicators.pattern:
title: Suspicious Outbound Telnet from IoT Device
id: 2b8c1f9a-5d7e-4b0c-8a1d-9e3f2a1b0c4d
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound network traffic on Telnet ports (23, 2323) which is highly suspicious for IoT devices and could indicate scanning activity by Mirai-like malware.
references:
  - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9VO5aom7I-w
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-15
tags:
  - attack.t1595
level: medium
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationPort:
      - 23
      - 2323
    Initiated: true
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects outbound network traffic on Telnet ports (23, 2323), which is a common behavior of Mirai variants scanning for new victims.

indicators.name: Potential DDoS Attack Traffic Pattern
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential DDoS Attack Traffic Pattern
id: e1d2c3b4-a5f6-4a90-8bcd-ef1234567890
status: experimental
description: Detects a high volume of outbound SYN, UDP, or HTTP floods, which is a classic sign of a device participating in a DDoS attack, characteristic of Mirai botnets.
references:
  - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9VO5aom7I-w
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-15
tags:
  - attack.t1498
level: high
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection_syn:
    action: 'allow'
    protocol: 'tcp'
    flags: 'S'
  selection_udp:
    action: 'allow'
    protocol: 'udp'
  timeframe: 10s
  condition: selection_syn or selection_udp | count() > 1000
indicators.description: Detects a high volume of outbound SYN or UDP traffic, which is characteristic of a device participating in a DDoS attack, the primary function of the Evooo1Bot botnet.
